_comment: Cached example output from a real run of ai_parser.parse_document() against sample_data/scrambled_expenses.csv, using claude-3-5-haiku-20241022. Bundled so `ai-data-clean demo` works without an API key.

line_items.notes: Trailing 'March' value likely indicates the expense month, not part of the amount.
Row used semicolons instead of commas as the field separator; date (2/14/2026) and category label ('office supply') were embedded in the text rather than in their own columns.

No dedicated conference/training category exists in the taxonomy; classified under Professional Services. Trailing note indicates this was paid personally by Suyog and may need reimbursement tracking.
Value is labeled as a monthly recurring rate (90.00/mo), not confirmed as a one-time charge for this report period.
Row used semicolons instead of commas as the field separator.
Amount is a self-reported estimate ('~20') because the receipt was lost; not an exact figure.
Could reasonably fall under Software & Subscriptions instead; classified as Marketing & Advertising since stock imagery is typically used in campaign creative.

issues: First row is a report title ('Expense Report - Q1 2026...') and was excluded as a header, not a line item.
Several fully blank or delimiter-only rows (e.g. ',,,,,' and ';;;;') were excluded.

The file mixes comma-delimited rows with a few semicolon-delimited rows, and column position for the amount is inconsistent row to row; amounts were located by content (currency-like values) rather than fixed column position.

Two rows (parking estimate, Google Workspace monthly rate) contain amounts that are explicitly approximate or recurring rather than exact one-time totals — flagged individually via low confidence and notes.
